articles.title: Nations League: Germany set up Netherlands clash after beating Serbia
articles.summary: Florian Wirtz on target in Germany’s 3-1 win in Serbia. Tijjani Reijnders hat-trick as Netherlands hammer Greece. Germany cruised to a 3-1 win against Serbia in Belgrade on Friday, setting up a crunch encounter with the Netherlands in Berlin on Monday to decide who tops Group A2.
body: In teeming rain in an almost empty stadium, the Germans forced Serbia’s Srdan Babic into an early own goal with Florian Wirtz and debutant Brajan Gruda also scoring.
Babic made up for his blunder with a second-half consolation strike, while Serbia finished with nine men after substitutes Vanja Dragojevic and Andrija Zivkovic were sent off late on.
Germany have now won twice, drawn twice and lost once in five games under coach Jürgen Klopp, who was optimistic the side were beginning to take shape under his tutelage.

“We played a truly fantastic game. I think we need to get a bit more used to the fact that we’re genuinely good – and capable of being very, very good,” Klopp told RTL. “Our counter-pressing was superb and the intensity was top-notch. So, from my point of view, it was a really, really good game.
points: Florian Wirtz on target in Germany’s 3-1 win in Serbia.

articles.title: France cling on for furious victory against South Africa after Dupont sizzles
articles.summary: France 21-19 South Africa. Scrum-half key in thriller full of twists and turns. The French had been waiting 21 years to see their team beat the Springboks at the Stade de France. In that time the team turned through successive generations and multiple iterations, risen, fallen and risen again.
body: What they did have, however, was Antoine Dupont. No fly-half? No problem. Earlier in the week their head coach, Fabien Galthié, had dismissed the idea that he and his opposite number, Rassie Erasmus, were playing mindgames with each other as “comic-book stuff”. Turns out this was just another bluff. Galthié had said Dupont was going to start at fly-half and, sure, he wore No 10 on his back, but he played the game in his usual position. It was his understudy Maxime Lucu who switched positions to play first receiver.

This was just one of the twists in a match full of them. There were a fistful of cards, some fantastic freewheeling tries, long stretches of intense scrummaging, a clutch of hugely controversial decisions by both coaches and the refereeing team and, at the very end of it all, one crucial missed kick, a conversion attempt by Manie Libbok that would have tied the scores with seven minutes left to play.
points: Scrum-half key in thriller full of twists and turns.
The French had been waiting 21 years to see their team beat the Springboks at the Stade de France.
What they did have, however, was Antoine Dupont.
Galthié had said Dupont was going to start at fly-half and, sure, he wore No 10 on his back, but he played the game in his usual position.

articles.title: John McGinn double saves Scotland’s blushes against North Macedonia
articles.summary: A special occasion for Andy Robertson saw Scotland flirt with embarrassment. Collection of his 102nd cap moves him level with Kenny Dalglish in the all-time Scottish list. Robertson will soon be a record holder. This was, however, John McGinn’s night.
body: This proved an almighty struggle for Scotland. Questions – and plenty of them – surround whether or not Sébastien Pocognoli can build on the excellent work of his predecessor Steve Clarke. For now, Scotland are a tough watch. Pocognoli looks tactically inflexible and this is not the new dawn many predicted.

“At times it wasn’t pretty,” admitted McGinn. The 32-year-old compared this Scotland process to a club team starting a new season. The rationale is fair enough, were this a remotely forgiving environment.

It was Robertson who led the dressing room inquest in the immediate aftermath of last month’s defeat to Slovenia. It is not in the Tottenham full-back’s make-up to personalise scenarios but shortcomings in the last international window, Pocognoli’s first as the Scotland manager, added to the sense that the bigger picture was important here. North Macedonia looked favourable visitors, having not scored a goal in eight outings.

articles.title: Jesús Owono given 12-match ban for tackle that resulted in Jesús de Miguel’s death
articles.summary: FC Andorra goalkeeper collided with De Miguel. Owono: ‘I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesús’ The FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono was suspended for 12 matches by the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee on Friday after his challenge on Jesús de Miguel resulted in the death of…
body: Owono, an Equatorial Guinea international, was sent off in the second division match on 2 November after racing into midfield and colliding with De Miguel while trying to clear an aerial ball. After the collision, De Miguel, 30, was placed in intensive care in hospital and the Spanish forward died on 3 November.

“The assessment of the conduct under consideration in these proceedings must be based on the facts expressly recorded in the referee’s report, which states that the player was sent off for ‘violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play,’” said the committee in a statement.

“The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesús de Miguel, is public knowledge. In view of the nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances … the maximum sanction, 12 matches of suspension, is justified.”
Spanish police sources said last week that an investigation into what happened had been opened under judicial supervision.

articles.title: Choi pushing for first LPGA win at The Annika as Korda drops back
articles.summary: Hye-Jin Choi opened with two bogeys, made up ground with a 15-foot eagle putt late and finished with a three-under 67 on Friday that gave her part of a three-way share of the lead at The Annika.
body: It was far more effective than the bogey-free round of Nelly Korda, the No. 1 player who could only laugh at her clean card because it was cleaner than she would have preferred - 15 straight pars, one birdie, two closing pars for a 69.
That left Korda four shots behind going into the weekend at Pelican Golf Club, where a victory would make the 28-year-old American eligible for the LPGA Hall of Fame.

"I had a lot of chances," said Korda, competing for the first time in two months. "But you can just tell that from yesterday morning to today afternoon with the wind, that's what the defence of this golf course is. It's as fast as Bermuda as I've putted on throughout my career."
It wasn't a problem for Solheim Cup star Carlota Ciganda, who birdied her last four holes for a 63 to join Choi and Lindy Duncan (66) atop the leaderboard at 12-under 128.

articles.title: Goalkeeper involved in fatal collision gets 12-game ban
articles.summary: Jesus Owono is given a 12-match suspension by the Spanish football federation's disciplinary committee after his challenge which resulted in the death of Jesus de Miguel.
body: FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been given a 12-match suspension by the Spanish football federation's disciplinary committee after his challenge which resulted in the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.
Owono, 25, was sent off after colliding with De Miguel during the closing stages of the second-tier match between their two respective sides on 2 November.

The disciplinary committee said it had to base its decision "on the facts expressly recorded in the referee's report", which stated the player "was sent off for 'violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play'.
"The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, is public knowledge."

articles.title: France put injuries behind them to stun Springboks
articles.summary: France put a raft of injuries behind them to withstand huge pressure and defeat South Africa 21-19 in a stunning Nations Championship victory in Paris.
body: The win is only the second for Les Bleus over the Springboks in the last 11 contests, with the hosts playing sensationally in the first half and digging in to survive and get over the line in the second.

Back-three Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang, Théo Attissogbe and Louis Bielle-Biarrey each scored tries in the opening half, with France belying the fact they had to play Antoine Dupont at 10 due to four fly-halves being out injured (Matthieu Jalibert, Romain Ntamack, Thomas Ramos, Antoine Hastoy).
All three tries were converted by Maxime Lucu, with France 21-7 ahead at the half-time break, but the second half proved entirely different.

articles.title: Salah scores twice as Egypt and Nigeria win Afcon 2027 qualifiers
articles.summary: Nigeria beat Tanzania to boost their hopes of reaching the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, while Mohamed Salah scores twice as Egypt cruise to victory over Malawi.
body: Tolu Arokodare was the hero as Nigeria boosted their hopes of reaching the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) with a 3-1 home win over tournament co-hosts Tanzania.

With the East Africans already assured of a spot at the finals, the Super Eagles are battling for the one qualification spot available in Group L and have little margin for error after losing 3-0 in Guinea-Bissau in September.
Alhassan Yusuf kept his composure to slot Nigeria into a second-minute lead in Uyo from Ademola Lookman's pass, but the visitors equalised through Alphonce Msanga just after the half-hour mark.
Arokodare climbed off the bench at half-time and cleverly flicked home Wilfred Ndidi's low ball to restore the lead for the West Africans in the 52nd minute.

articles.summary: Max Dowman broke Jude Bellingham's record to become the youngest player to represent England at U21 level but could not stop Lee Carsley's side from falling to a 1-0 loss against Portugal.
body: Dowman, aged 16, 10 months and 13 days, stepped off the bench with around half an hour remaining to make his debut, but Moreira's first half strike secured the victory for Portugal on the evening.

Lee Carsley's side have now suffered successive defeats for the first time since March 2021 following their loss to the Republic of Ireland in their last European Championship qualifying match in October.
England's preparations for next year's tournament did not get off to an ideal start as Bayer Leverkusen forward Moreira put the visitors ahead at the break.

Portugal's superiority continued in the second half and the hosts had to rely on a string of Tommy Setford saves to keep them in the contest, but the Arsenal goalkeeper could not stop them from falling to defeat.

articles.title: WTA Finals: Svitolina defeats Sabalenka to reach semi-finals
articles.summary: Elina Svitolina defeated Aryna Sabalenka over three compelling sets to reach the semi-finals of the WTA Finals in Indian Wells.
body: The Ukrainian won 6-3 ⁠3-6 ​6-1, standing up to Sabalenka's powerful serve as she won the first set.
Sabalenka stormed back to take control of the second set. But momentum shifted yet again in the deciding set.
The opening games of the third were tight, but Svitolina landed a hammer blow when she broke Sabalenka's service game to go 3-1 up and pressed on from there to run away with the final set.
"Very happy with the performance. It was not an easy match. It was a little bit of a roller coaster," Svitolina told Sky Sports.

articles.title: How A Sudden FAA Ground Stop Could Affect CFB, NFL This Weekend
articles.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration's decision to ground all flights nationwide Friday threw the sports world into chaos, leaving NBA, NHL and college teams stranded as they tried to reach their destinations, and NFL teams were left to wonder whether the issue would be resolved in time for them to…
body: The FAA issued a notice that said the ground stop was "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety."

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy later said there was a communications issue affecting the 22 regional air traffic control centers that direct planes en route between airports nationwide, and that FAA technicians were investigating.
"There’s no reason to be concerned about your loved ones if they’re flying," Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin said.

Most college football teams playing Saturday travel the day before their game, and the stoppage left many schools — including No. 2 Utah, eighth-ranked Texas and No. 9 Tennessee — at a standstill as they departed for road games. The Utes play at No. 22 Arizona, the Longhorns visit No. 24 LSU and the Vols are traveling to Texas A&M in three of the bigger games of the weekend.
